INTERVENOR GEORGE NOELKE’S OBJECTION AND MOTION TO STRIKE APPLICANTS’
                     "DIRECTORY OF EVIDENCE"

TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

George Noelke, Intervenor in 59475 and 59182, files this Objection and Motion to Strike Applicants’
Directory of Evidence of Preliminary Order Issue Nos. 11 and 13 (the "Directory"), filed on September
21, 2026, and respectfully shows the following:




                                                                                                        1
 I. Background

A. On June 10, 2026 the ALJs issued their PFD in 59182. See Item 537. (Noelke specially appears in this
docket, preserving his jurisdiction arguments, in view of his ongoing objection that the lapse of the
180-day deadline in 59182 deprives SOAH and the PUC of subject matter jurisdiction.) On August 20,
2026, the ALJs issued their PFD for the above-captioned consolidated dockets on the issue of need. See
Item 6441. The PFD in Docket No. 59475 recommended the denial of the applications in 59475 and
59182.

B. On September 18, 2026, the PUC issued its Order Remanding Proceeding to SOAH. See Items 6578 in
59475 and 612 in 59182. The Commission directed the ALJs on remand to address Preliminary Order
Issue Nos. 11 (compliance with reliability standards) and 13 (consumer congestion cost savings) in a
supplemental or amended PFD pursuant to 16 TAC § 22.262(c).​

C. On September 15, 2026, the ALJs issued SOAH Order No. 34 (Notice to the Parties), confirming their
intention to prepare and issue a supplemental PFD on the limited issues identified by the Commission.
The ALJs did not reopen the evidentiary record, did not invite briefing, and did not set a supplemental
briefing schedule. See Item 6569 in 59475. A companion Order was not filed in 59182.​

D. On September 21, 2026, without seeking leave and without procedural authorization, Applicants filed
a 22-page document entitled Applicants' Directory of Evidence of Preliminary Order Issue Nos. 11 and
13. See Items 6593 in 59475 and 615 in 59182.

II. Grounds for Striking the Submission

A. The Submission Is an Unauthorized, Unilateral Post-Hearing Brief
Applicants attempt to minimize this filing by styling it as an administrative "directory" submitted merely
for the ALJs' "convenience." In reality, it is a 22-page, substantive post-hearing brief submitted after the
evidentiary record closed and after the initial post-hearing briefing cycle concluded.

Contested case procedures before SOAH do not permit parties to file unsolicited briefs during the
tribunal's internal drafting process. The ALJs in SOAH Order No. 34, filed only in 59475, provided
notice that they would draft the supplemental PFD on the existing record; they did not solicit argument,
executive summaries, or curated evidentiary indices from any party. Applicants' filing violates established
SOAH procedures governing post-hearing schedules (1 TAC 155.305(a) and 155.505; 16 TAC § 22.202).
Moreover, the Intervenors in 59182 are without the guidance of the limitations set in SOAH Order No. 34
because a companion Order was not filed in 59182.

B. The Submission Constitutes Ex Parte-Style Advocacy and Violates Procedural Fairness
Under the Texas Administrative Procedure Act (Tex. Gov't Code § 2001.051) and 16 TAC § 22.202(d), all
parties are entitled to full notice and equal opportunity to respond to submissions made to the tribunal.
Specifically, 2001.051(2) provides, “In a contested case, each party is entitled to an opportunity…
to respond and to present evidence and argument on each issue involved in the case.” Emphasis added.




                                                                                                               2
 The “Directory" is far from neutral. It is an overtly argumentative compilation that:
   1.​ Characterizes evidence under argumentative legal headers (e.g., claiming ERCOT assessments
       are "Entitled to Great Weight")1;
   2.​ Isolates selective, self-serving excerpts of Applicants' direct and rebuttal testimony; and
   3.​ Omits all opposing evidence, critical witness cross-examination, party admissions, and intervenor
       testimony undermining those claims.

Allowing Applicants to unilaterally submit 22 pages of selective argumentation to the ALJs while in the
middle of drafting an amended PFD—without authorization, schedule, or an automatic right of
reply—violates fundamental administrative fairness.

C. The Submission Circumvents the Statutory Process for Exceptions to a Supplemental PFD
Under 16 TAC § 22.262(c)(2), the PUC procedural rules provide an explicit, orderly mechanism for
parties to address the issues on remand: filing Exceptions to the Supplemental Proposal for Decision.

If Applicants believe that the closed evidentiary record contains evidence satisfying their burden of proof
on Preliminary Order Issue Nos. 11 and 13, the lawful forum to make that argument is in their written
Exceptions after the supplemental PFD is issued. Applicants cannot short-circuit this statutory procedure
by filing a preemptive brief to influence the ALJs' findings before the supplemental PFD is even drafted.

D. The Directory Confirms the Evidentiary Absence Regarding Issue 13
Even if the ALJs were to examine the submission, it demonstrates the exact evidentiary defect identified
by Intervenors:
    1.​ To support Issue 13 (consumer congestion savings), Applicants cite general ERCOT system-wide
        congestion figures from 2023-2024, general comparative studies of the 765-kV STEP plan across
        the entire ERCOT grid, and qualitative statements that 765-kV lines lower costs.
    2.​ Applicants fail to cite a single quantitative study, simulation, or dollar figure in the record that
        calculates or estimates the consumer congestion cost savings attributable specifically to the Bell
        County East to Big Hill segment (Docket No. 59475) or the Big Hill to Sand Lake segment
        (Docket No. 59182).

Applicants' attempt to substitute macro-level system commentary for project-specific proof confirms that
no such evidence was ever introduced into the record.


E. Procedural Disparity and Exploitation of the Omission of Order No. 34 in Docket No. 59182

Applicants’ submission in Docket No. 59182 suffers from a fatal procedural defect: it relies upon an
interlocutory SOAH order that does not legally exist in that docket’s record. While the Commission
remanded both proceedings to SOAH on September 18, 2026, the ALJs’ September 15, 2026 notice of



1
 Noelke in fact challenged Applicants’ interpretation of “great weight” in both his Exceptions and Replies to
Exceptions in 59475. See Items 6480 and 6539. Exceptions and Replies to Exceptions are the proper pleading to
make such legal arguments.


                                                                                                                3
 intent to draft a supplemental PFD was issued exclusively as SOAH Order No. 34 in Docket No. 59475.
No companion order or joint directive was entered or served in Docket No. 59182.

Because these dockets were consolidated only to a limited extent and retain distinct identities, parties, and
records, the omission of a companion order leaves Docket No. 59182 in procedural limbo2 and deprives
59182-only parties of official notice under Texas Government Code § 2001.051. Applicants nevertheless
filed Item No. 615 directly into Docket No. 59182, citing SOAH Order No. 34 as their sole justification
for submitting this 22-page compilation. A party cannot manufacture procedural standing or justification
to file supplemental, unsolicited advocacy in Docket No. 59182 by piggybacking on an order entered
exclusively in a separate docket. Filing this uninvited material into a docket that lacks even an operative
SOAH scheduling or status order violates 16 TAC §§ 22.71–.74, denies equal opportunity to respond
under Tex. Gov’t Code § 2001.051(2), and requires that the submission be stricken from Docket No.
59182.

III. Prayer

WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDERED, Intervenor respectfully requests that the Administrative
Law Judges:

1. GRANT this Motion and STRIKE Applicants' Directory of Evidence of Preliminary Order Issue Nos.
11 and 13 (Item No. 615 in Docket No. 59182 / Item No. 6593 in Docket No. 59475) from the record in
both proceedings as an unauthorized and untimely post-hearing pleading;

2. STRIKE the submission from Docket No. 59182 specifically on the independent ground that it
improperly purports to execute and rely upon an order (SOAH Order No. 34) that was never entered,
issued, or noticed in Docket No. 59182;

3. IN THE ALTERNATIVE, enter an order, or rule in the supplemental PFD for 59475, confirming that
the ALJs will not and did not review, consider, or rely upon the Directory in drafting the Supplemental
Proposal for Decision; and



2
  Note that Noelke filed an objection to Delaware Basin’s Exceptions and Replies in 59475 because they are a party
in 59182 but not a party in 59475. See Item 6539 in 59475 at p.3. Note also that in 59182 Texas Scottish Rite
Hospital and other Intervenors filed a letter requesting clarification concerning the impact of the limited
consolidation on Intervenors in 59182. In that letter, Mr. Harris raised the following 4 questions, none of which are
answered on the record in either 59182 or 59475: “1. Are all intervenors in Docket No. 59182 now intervenors in
Docket No. 59475, and, therefore, free to participate in examining witnesses on the "need issue" and to submit
briefing on that issue? 2. Does the failure of an intervenor in Docket No. 59182 to participate in Docket No. 59475
on the "need issue" have any impact on the applicability of a decision on need to the non-participating party? 3.
Does the consolidation affect when a PFD will be issued in Docket No. 59182? 4. Does the consolidation change
when the Public Utility Commission will consider the PFD in Docket No 59182 given that a decision on need could
affect whether the Public Utility Commission addresses route selection?” And, with Applicants’ “directory” filing in
59475 and 59182, an additional question that should be answered is: Can the Applicants, on remand, selectively
leverage their interpretation of purported record evidence in 59475 to their advantage in 59182 when that purported
record evidence was never admitted in 59182 and thereby was never challenged by 59182 Intervenors? Clearly, the
answer to this question should be “No,” especially during a remand proceeding with the four questions above left
unanswered.


                                                                                                                   4
 4. IN THE FURTHER ALTERNATIVE, if the ALJs determine that the Directory will be considered, enter
a formal procedural order in both dockets granting Intervenors and all other non-applicant parties a period
of at least fourteen (14) days to file a responsive counter-directory and rebuttal citations to the record
pursuant to Texas Government Code § 2001.051(2).

Intervenor prays for all other and further relief to which he may be entitled.

Signed: September 22, 2026


Respectfully submitted,

​
George Noelke​
George Noelke​
Intervenor​
Pro se Landowner

George Noelke​
